chunks: My father (rah) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us from 'Imran ibn Musa from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Hamad ibn Uthman from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said: I said to Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
What is the meaning of His saying, Exalted and Blessed is He: 'Who is it that will offer Allah a goodly loan, so He will multiply it for him manifold?'

He said: It is maintaining ties with the Imam. My father (rah) said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Fadl narrated to us from Abu Talib Abdillah ibn al-Salt from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ishaq ibn Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) with a similar one.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic verse 'Who is it that will offer Allah a goodly loan' mean according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a specific exegetical link between the Quranic metaphor of 'lending Allah a goodly loan' (64:17) and the act of *silat* (maintaining ties of kinship and goodness) towards the Imam. This interpretation elevates the spiritual status of the Imam, framing devotion to him as a direct investment in the Divine, thereby guaranteeing multiplied rewards. The presence of a second, independent chain of transmission (*isnad*) in the text underscores the reliability and scholarly acceptance of this specific theological understanding within Shia tradition.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to us by Ahmad b. Idris from ’Imran b. Musa from Ya’qub b. Yazid from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Abi Nasr from Hamad b. Uthman from Ishaq b. Ammar who said: The narrator asked Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.),
“What is the meaning of this verse: ‘Who is it that will offer of Allah a goodly gift, so He will multiply it to him manifold’?”10
Imam (a.s.) replied, “It implies doing good to an Imam.” The narrator says that his father too heard such a tradition from Imam (a.s.).
